correctness.rationale: Independent interval bond probabilities and counting ordered pairs give expected loss 1+2F/n. Singleton interval terms alone make the Hessian positive in every nonzero direction; compactness gives a unique reflection-invariant optimum. Convexity makes the simplex derivative comparison both necessary and sufficient. In the even center solution, the inactive-to-active difference at edge k<m is (m-k)(mq-k) with q=e^(-B); in the odd solution it is (m-k)(q+mq^2-k) with q=e^(-B/2), because crossing pairs reach the center vertex with one attenuation and the opposite block with two. In each case k=m-1 controls; the odd margin factors at that edge as (q+1)(mq-(m-1)). Thus both exact cutoffs follow, and a strictly downhill feasible move exists above each. Strict convexity handles ties at the cutoffs, and reflection handles n=3. The removed four-site equation was itself correct: differentiating the reduced three-term variable-dependent sum gives e^B=e^(3x)+e^(2x), with the optimizer interior above log 2.
residual_risks: Analytic certificate is all-size; the supplied checker is finite and includes a floating grid for the illustrative four-site specialization. No general later activation theorem is evaluated.
